sourceFacts: Most otitis media with effusion resolves without intervention, but persistent effusion beyond three months should trigger hearing assessment and ENT involvement.
Hearing difficulty matters even if speech development appears normal; management depends on the child's hearing and clinical context.
prompt:
Create an entirely original medical teaching concept illustration, landscape 3:2, warm hand-painted watercolour and gouache on ivory paper, fine ink contours, restrained navy labels, muted teal, ochre and peach accents, generous whitespace. Gentle storybook warmth with the precision and legibility of an educational atlas. Use written instructions only; no image reference. Meaningful visual relationships and sparse short labels, not paragraphs in boxes. NO internal anatomy, organ/eye/ear/brain/tissue cutaways, anatomical pathways, bones, diagnostic images, fake scans, realistic lesions, photorealistic skin, glossy wet flesh or 3D tissue. Neutral symbols or fully clothed surface poses only where specified. Preserve every direction, relationship and count in the explicit structure. Title and labels exactly as requested, no additional prose. Footer 'Educational schematic'. No logo or watermark.

Title 'Persistent fluid: check hearing'. A long horizontal calendar strip begins LEFT with a symbolic blue drop labelled 'Effusion'. Teal time arrow runs to a highlighted calendar milestone at centre labelled 'Beyond 3 months'; no dates, no fictional patient data. From milestone a broad rightward arrow reaches a large pair of headphones on a plain stand labelled 'Hearing assessment', then a short arrow to an 'ENT review' appointment card. Below timeline a small speech bubble containing a simple star sits beside text 'Speech may still seem normal'. No audiogram, hearing threshold number, ear anatomy or automatic surgery arrow. This is persistent effusion follow-up, not a rule to wait when urgent clinical concerns exist.
